subject: Media Literacy
title: Teaching Children About Ads
description: A quick, practical guide to Teaching Children About Ads.

hook.text: A six-year-old can't tell the difference between a cartoon and a toy commercial. Advertisers know this.

buildup.text: Children lack the cognitive ability to recognize persuasive intent in advertising until around age eight.

discovery.text: Teaching children to ask 'who made this and why' builds critical skills that protect them from manipulation.

twist.text: Digital ads targeting children are harder to spot than TV commercials — games, influencers, and apps blur the line.

climax.text: Ad literacy is a life skill. The earlier children learn it, the stronger their defenses grow.

punchline.text: Teach kids to spot ads early. It's a defense they'll need forever.

quiz.question: At what age can children typically recognize persuasive intent in ads?
